mappedContracts.statement: Redact and classify sensitive data structurally before any value reaches console, logs, MCP output, traces, fixtures, errors, or CI artefacts.
acceptanceCriteria: No raw arbitrary error string is persisted.
Correlation uses one-way fingerprints rather than partial secret disclosure.
Run-log privacy levels default to minimal.
Secret-scanner tests use synthetic credentials only.

mappedContracts.statement: Maintain an evidence-backed threat model for CLI, browser, internal API, official API, MCP stdio, MCP HTTP, registry distribution, state storage, and supply-chain boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Threats include credential exfiltration, SSRF, prompt/argument injection, path traversal, confused deputy, replay, duplicate mutation, supply-chain compromise, PII leakage, and malicious repository content.
Each threat maps to controls, tests, residual risk, and owner.
The model is reviewed for each release.

mappedContracts.statement: Implement mature supply-chain controls: immutable action SHAs, CodeQL, dependency review, actionlint, zizmor, OpenSSF Scorecard, maintained secret scanning, OSV scanning, licence policy, npm signature audit, SBOMs, provenance, and signed attestations.
acceptanceCriteria: All applicable checks are required and least-privilege.
The bespoke secret scanner is removed or reduced to synthetic project-specific policy on top of a maintained scanner.
SPDX and CycloneDX SBOMs preserve unique package identities and dependency relationships.
